A soot-blackened hearth roars amber at the room's heart, its embers pulsing like drowsy eyes, while a single tallow candle gutters on the mantle above, pooling wax across cracked stone.
Three floating wisp-orbs drift near the ceiling, trailing cool blue luminescence, their glow caught and warmed by a fat beeswax candelabra standing seven-branched on the reading desk below.
Glowing crystals veined through the cave wall shed a slow violet radiance, their cold light softened by a clay oil-lamp set in a natural shelf, flame bending in unseen drafts.
A brass oil-lantern hangs from a low rafter beam, its perforated cap throwing star-patterned shadows across rough timber walls, the wick trimmed short and burning honey-warm.
Luminescent moss carpets the hollow's curved ceiling in pale seafoam green, while a hearthstone at floor level breathes orange heat upward, the two lights meeting in a wash of warm jade.
Runic engravings carved along the observatory walls pulse with slow amber light, supplemented by a suspended iron chandelier holding twelve tallow candles dripping in uneven ivory columns.
A dragon-flame sealed inside a hammered brass urn casts fierce gold across the war-chamber, the overflow of its heat softened at the room's edges by a cluster of mushrooms glowing soft coral-pink.
Two oil-lanterns bracketed to stone flanking the fireplace burn steady and low, while the hearth behind them roars with split oak, the doubled warmth turning the whole study a deep burnished copper.

Luminous flora—night-blooming silver-thread vines—wind around the hollow's entrance posts, their cold white glow feeding inward and meeting a small iron brazier packed with cherry-red coals at the chamber's center.
A leaded-glass window set with magically luminous panes throws colored lozenges of teal and amber across the floor, the pattern shifting as a candle behind the glass burns slowly down its holder.

Floating candle-flames—six in all, unmoored from any wick or holder—circle the apothecary shelf lazily, casting warm moving shadows, while a single glowing crystal-orb on the counter holds the room's cooler undertone.
Fireplace embers banked low breathe a red-orange pulse through iron grating, barely enough to read by, so a brass oil-lantern on its tall stand leans close to the open book like an attentive servant.

Glowing mushrooms the size of fists line the stone passage in alternating gold and blue, their bioluminescence steady and unhurried, giving the druid-hollow the calm quality of light seen through shallow water.
A single fat church candle burns on a wooden spike beside the hermit's cot, the flame enormous and steady in still air, its wax body half-consumed and amber with the smoke of years.

Pulsing rune-light traces every seam of the vault's stone blocks in cold green, while an oil-lantern with a cracked horn panel sits on the floor nearby, leaking warm yellow through the fracture in uneven stripes.

A chandelier of antler and iron holds twenty candles above the longhouse table, their collective warmth filling the rafters with honey-colored smoke haze, a second source glowing from a crystal-orb in the center of the table.

Wisp-orbs in a corked glass jar pulse softly blue on the windowsill, their trapped light unreliable and dreamy, while the woodstove across the room radiates steady amber from its iron belly through a half-open grate.

Glowing crystals arranged in a deliberate ring on the floor emit slow rose-gold light upward, illuminating the underside of the alchemist's face as she works, a brass lantern hung overhead adding its own steadier warmth.

Hearth-fire fills the lower half of the cottage in amber and shadow while above, a luminous moth-wing pendant—enchanted, softly glowing pale white—hangs from a ceiling hook, lighting the top shelves the fire cannot reach.

Four tallow candles on a pewter plate cluster around an open tome, their combined flame creating a small sun above the text, while deep in the corner a crack in the wall leaks runic cold-light from the room beyond.

An iron brazier full of charcoal burns steady and smokeless at the room's center, casting even amber heat, while luminescent moss pressed behind framed glass on each wall adds a background cool green glow.

A smoking oil-lamp with a clay belly and a trimmed rush wick sits beside the mortar, its small warm flame intimate and close, the rest of the root-cellar cave lit by glowing mushrooms massed along the lower walls.

Floating wisp-orbs cluster near the observatory's domed ceiling like cool captive stars, their pale silver light useful for star-charts, while a single brass candelabra on the instrument table burns warm below for close reading work.

Fireplace embers glow tiger-orange behind an iron screen, the room mostly dim, until a glowing crystal-orb on the mantle brightens in response to movement, its blue-white radiance layering over the ember-warmth in shifting lavender.

A pair of oil-lanterns with green-glass panels hang from shepherd's hooks flanking the apothecary door, flooding the entry with warm emerald, their light mixing with the cool pulsing rune-glow etched into the door's stone arch above.
A low iron hearth bleeds amber firelight across stone walls while three pale wisp-orbs drift near the rafters, their cold silver glow layering over the warm ember-flush below.
Clusters of luminescent cave-mushrooms pulse a soft blue-green from mossy ledges while a single brass oil-lantern hanging from a root-beam casts a honey-warm pool across the earthen floor.
A fat beeswax candle melts inside a leaded-glass lantern, its flame doubling in the beveled panes, and runic carvings along the doorframe answer with a slow amber-gold throb.
A stone hearth roars with split-oak fire, and wedged into the mortar above it a thumb-sized glowing crystal bleeds violet light that wars beautifully with the orange hearthglow.

Floating candle-flames, untethered and drifting, bob gently near the ceiling like lazy fireflies, their individual warm halos bleeding together overhead while embers pulse red-orange in the grate below.
